{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Spot FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and recommended redlines

## Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the draft Agreement. Eighteen rules were assessed: five clauses are compliant, ten are deviations requiring redlines, and three rules are unaddressed in the document (termination for convenience, transition assistance and data return, and Vendor insurance).

The risk is concentrated and structurally one-sided in the Licensor's favour. Eight findings sit in walk-away territory: there is no Licensor IP indemnity at all (Article XII is a one-way Licensee indemnity, and Article XIII states that "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE" for third-party infringement claims); the liability cap is one-sided at one half of amounts paid while our liability is uncapped with no carve-outs; the Licensor may assign freely while we may not, and any Change of Control of Licensee automatically terminates the Agreement and all licences; we are committed to a 36-month Initial Period with no convenience exit, while the Licensor holds a unilateral option to extend by a further seven years; the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed; audits may be demanded without frequency limit or advance notice; and there is no insurance covenant despite the Licensor hosting the Platform and processing our trade data.

Ownership is also adverse: enhancements and customisation work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in the Licensor as Derivative Works, our licence is non-exclusive, non-modifiable, non-transferable and terminates with the Agreement, and there is no limitation on the Licensor's use of data we supply. Separately, Article XXII imposes a first-refusal/right-to-match mechanic over any third-party offer for our assets or a merger, on five business days' notice.

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, and no liquidated damages or early-termination charge on us, and governing law and venue (New York law; exclusive SDNY and New York State courts, with no arbitration clause) sit at our preferred position.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Articles XII–XIII) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Article XIII) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS (Articles XXIV(c), XX(a)) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Article IV(b) (fee table, "50+ US$5.00") |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Article XXII) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Article X(b)) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Article IV) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (after Article XXI) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER (Article VIX) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS |

## Walk-away items

These eight findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity (INDEMN).** Article XII is a one-way Licensee indemnity, and Article XIII disclaims all Licensor liability for third-party infringement. We add a Licensor IP indemnity at the fallback level — customary Licensee modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace and refund remedies, and a 3x annual fees super-cap — and conform Article XIII so the indemnity is not negated. We leave the existing Licensee indemnity in place.
2. **One-sided cap below floor (LOL-CAP).** Article XIII caps only the Licensor, at one half of amounts paid (below six months' fees), while our liability, including the broad Article XII indemnity, is uncapped with no carve-outs. We target the fallback: mutual cap at 12 months' fees, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. The one-sided consequential-damages exclusion in clause (a) and clause (c) are noted for negotiation but not redlined.
3. **Assignment and Change of Control (ASSIGN).** Article XXIV(c) bars any Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out while the Licensor may assign freely, including to our competitors; Article XX(a) makes any Change of Control of Licensee an automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences. We move to the preferred position: affiliate and successor assignment without consent, Licensor assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, and removal of the Change of Control termination right.
4. **No Customer convenience exit in a 36-month term (T4C).** No provision permits us to terminate for convenience. We insert the preferred position: 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the term.
5. **Unilateral seven-year renewal (RENEWAL).** Article IV lets the Licensor extend the Initial Period by a further seven years with no Licensee opt-out or notice window. We delete the option so renewal requires mutual written agreement.
6. **"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed (WARRANTY).** Article VIX disclaims all warranties and expressly disclaims that nonconformity to Documentation will be corrected; Article VII(f) Error Corrections is not a warranty and carries no remedy. We redline to the fallback: 90-day software conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, repair/replacement or refund, and an express carve-out from both disclaimer sentences.
7. **Unlimited audit rights (AUDIT).** Article IV(b) permits audits at any frequency, and the 30-day reference is our deadline to permit the audit rather than advance notice. Cost allocation (Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found) and the independent CPA requirement already meet the preferred position; we add frequency, notice, business-hours, off-site, auditor confidentiality and no-system-access limits.
8. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** The only reference to insurance is a pass-through of charges payable by us. Given the Licensor hosts the Platform and processes our trade data, we insert a covenant at the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M; cyber and privacy USD 2M), and would accept the preferred CGL/E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M package.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten deviations and three missing clauses, opening at the positions recorded above. Where we have drafted to the fallback (IP licence-back and data-use limitation; mutual 12-month cap; Licensor IP indemnity; 90/30-day warranties; insurance limits; affiliate and successor licence rights), we should state the fallback on the face of the comment so the Licensor understands the concession already made.
2. **Escalate the eight walk-away items** to the business owner before the next call. Recommended non-negotiables: a Licensor IP indemnity, a mutual cap with carve-outs, a Customer convenience exit, removal of the unilateral seven-year renewal, and deletion of the automatic termination on our Change of Control.
3. **Confirm the two repaired redlines** — MFN (Article XXII first-refusal/matching mechanic, with the follow-on sentence restated to carry its own antecedent and subordinated to the retained Change of Control and Assignment provisions) and NOSOLICIT (Article X(b) narrowed to mutual, 12 months, involved personnel only, retaining the favourable carve-out sentence verbatim) — read cleanly against the retained text before the draft goes out.
4. **Note for the business, without redlining:** the Field of Use excludes any functions or applications not expressly described, so any future non-Spot FX use of the Platform will require a scope amendment; and the Supplemental Payments revenue share (33% of third-party amounts earned from use of the Licensed Technology) is an economic term for commercial review rather than a legal deviation.
5. **Do not reopen the compliant items** (exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitments, liquidated damages, governing law and venue); they sit at our preferred position and are helpful trading stock in the negotiation."}
